text:
support-lucy: Customer on dedicated-prod-eu2 reporting sudden tail latency spikes from ~80ms to >1.2s around 11:12 UTC. They say this started after a large batch job earlier today. :rotating_light:

infra-bot: ALERT: pool=dedicated-prod-eu2 node=node-eu2-gpu-07 gpu_util=98% mem_util=92% MIG_PARTS=3/3 link=https://infra.company/alerts/AL-9821

tom-chen: looking. which customer? any request ids or sample API calls?

support-lucy: customer id=acme-ml, sample req_id=rdw_req_20250101_8421. They sent high-concurrency synchronous calls to text-generate (model: redwood-v2-8b) with concurrency=10 and token_limit=1024.

raj: possible noisy neighbor / MIG oversubscription. can you grab node-level nvml and pod metrics?

elaine: adding quick checks:
```
kubectl get pods -n dedicated-acme -o wide | grep acme
kubectl top pod -n dedicated-acme --containers
rdwctl node-metrics node-eu2-gpu-07 --export nvml.log
```

support-lucy: did those, attaching snips: 
```
# kubectl top (trimmed)
pod/acme-batcher  92% GPU
pod/acme-infer-0  84% GPU
pod/rdw-shared-0  99% GPU
```
Also nvml shows one MIG partition with sustained SM % > 95 for 20m.

tom-chen: that rdw-shared-0 is suspicious. Is it a long-running heavy batch on same node?

support-lucy: yes customer says they launched a throughput job that pinned to the pool earlier and requested burst autoscaling.

raj: two angles: 1) confirm MIG partitioning is configured to isolate tenants; 2) check scheduler/allocator didn't pack latency-sensitive pods on same MIG slice.

elaine: quick config checks:
```
rdwctl get-pool-config dedicated-prod-eu2 --json
# look for enable_mig_sharing, placement_policy
```

infra-bot: POOL_CONFIG: dedicated-prod-eu2 {"enable_mig_sharing": true, "placement_policy": "binpack", "autoscaler": {"scale_up_cooldown": 30, "max_burst": 2}}

sre-eli: enable_mig_sharing=true + binpack = recipe for noisy neighbor if autoscaler pins batch jobs. we should consider: set enable_mig_sharing=false for this pool, or change placement_policy to spread for latency-tier customers.

tom-chen: can we repro in staging? i can spin up the same batcher job against a staging node with identical MIG config and run concurrent small-latency traffic. runbook:
```
# reproduce
rdw-cli invoke --host staging-eu2 --model redwood-v2-8b --concurrency 10 --tokens 1024 --qps 120 --duration 10m
kubectl run load-batch --image=rdw/batcher:canary --env CONCURRENCY=12 --replicas=1
rdwctl monitor latency --req-id sample
```

support-lucy: i've told the customer: we recommend moving latency-critical pods to a dedicated isolated pool while we investigate. they accepted temporary move.

raj: for long-term: add placement_policy=spread for pools with mix of batch+serving OR enforce enable_mig_sharing=false for latency tiers. also autoscaler: reduce max_burst or tag burst capacity to separate nodes.

elaine: I'll open infra ticket and schedule config change on a maintenance window. moving to P1 since customer is in enterprise tier and impact is tail latency >1s.

sre-eli: steps I'm taking now:
- cordon node-eu2-gpu-07 and drain rdw-shared-0
- evict heavy batcher to new node with MIG sharing allowed
- flip enable_mig_sharing=false on dedicated-prod-eu2 (in staging first)
- gather nvml logs + p95/p99 before/after

infra-bot: TICKET CREATED: INF-1157 linked to AL-9821. assigned: elaine, tom-chen. ETA first update 30m.

tom-chen: i'll run the staging repro and post traces. if we confirm, we should add a guard in allocator to avoid putting high-throughput batch pods into same MIG slice as latency-critical pods.

support-lucy: customer moved to isolated pool, reported p95 back down to ~95ms after move. they want root cause and a plan to avoid recurrence.

elaine: noted. collecting root-cause artifacts (nvml, kube events, allocator logs) and will update ticket.

sre-eli: thanks everyone. draft for postmortem once we have artifacts: cause = MIG sharing + binpack + autoscaler burst; mitigation = change defaults for latency pools, allocator guardrails, autoscaler limits, and customer-facing guidance on burst workload placement.

support-lucy: closing loop with customer and copying them to ticket. :white_check_mark:

tom-chen: posting link to repro playbook in ticket when done.
